methodology: Bounded first-pass narrative/relationship screening using Qur'anic passage content and adjacent Q11:84–90 context. No authenticated original-language external textual parallel, epigraphic witness or critical edition established this session. Negative classifications are provisional, not proof of absence.

verses.summary: Shuʿayb's opponents claim not to understand much of his speech, call him weak and say his clan prevents them from stoning him.
verses.caveat: Potential general prophetic-rejection and clan-protection motifs are insufficient to establish a source-specific predecessor.

verses.summary: Shuʿayb asks whether his clan is more esteemed than God and condemns placing God behind their backs.
verses.caveat: No precise pre-Islamic primary passage checked that reproduces the social exchange.

verses.summary: Shuʿayb challenges the people to act according to their position and anticipates a humiliating punishment.
verses.caveat: Threat-and-vindication rhetoric is widespread; no direct earlier parallel verified.

verses.summary: When divine command comes, Shuʿayb and believers are rescued by mercy while a blast seizes the wrongdoers.
verses.caveat: The Arabic term ṣayḥa and rescue/judgment pattern require careful comparison with other Qur'anic accounts before external parallels; no Biblical Midian destruction narrative is established.

verses.summary: The destroyed inhabitants lie motionless as though they had never flourished; Madyan is dismissed like Thamūd.
verses.caveat: Comparative destruction formula is not independently traceable here to a specific earlier passage.

dossier.title: Shuʿayb and Madyan: rejection, protection and judgment

sections.background: The Qur'anic narrative links economic injustice, religious rejection and the social standing of Shuʿayb's clan. Identification with Biblical Midian and Jethro is a research question, not an established identity.
sections.chronology: The Qur'an is a seventh-century text. Dates for the narrative setting and any independently documented historical Madyan community must be established separately from the date of Qur'anic composition; no manuscript witness was collated here.
sections.comparative_discussion: The sequence moves from a threatened prophet protected by clan solidarity (11:91–92) to challenge (11:93) and collective destruction, with rescue of believers (11:94–95). A loose prophetic-rejection motif alone does not establish literary dependence.
sections.variant_witnesses: No pre-Islamic primary-text witness for this specific Shuʿayb episode verified. No source may be promoted on the basis of an English keyword match.
sections.scholarly_interpretations: Potential connections with Biblical Midian, Jethro and general ancient Near Eastern justice traditions remain hypotheses requiring distinct textual, geographical and chronological argument.
